verdict.rationale: Claude Code documents Hooks: user-defined shell commands that run automatically before or after Claude Code actions, such as auto-formatting after every file edit. It also documents MCP channels that push webhook events into a session so Claude reacts to them, and automatic code review on every PR. However, the evidence is only one-line overview mentions, with no detail on the rule definition format, event catalog, matching conditions, or independent corroboration. Missing for 10: documented hook event types and configuration/matcher syntax, conditional rule logic, depth on event-driven triggers beyond Claude's own actions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Hooks let you run shell commands before or after Claude Code actions, like auto-formatting after every file edit or running lint before a commit.
an MCP server can also act as a channel that pushes messages into your session, so Claude reacts to Telegram messages, Discord chats, or webhook events while you're away
